candidates.name: predicthq/sdk-py
candidates.what_it_holds: Official Python client (MIT, 27 stars, updated May 2026) for the PredictHQ Events API, which categorizes real-world events by date/location/rank including conferences, expos, festivals, concerts, sports, public/school holidays, community and political events, severe weather and disasters. No data is committed in the repo itself, but the client makes conference/expo/MICE-type event counts and predicted attendance-impact scores pullable per city per week -- the closest thing found on GitHub to a queryable MICE/conference-calendar feed relevant to ABNB's corporate/urban demand markets. Free tier exists (rate-limited); full historical backfill and higher categories are paid.
candidates.why_useful: Fills gap #11 (events and shocks) and the MICE/conference-calendar keyword directly -- a per-city, per-week conference/expo signal is exactly the kind of business-travel demand proxy the theme is chasing, though it is a paid-tiered acquisition method rather than a free static dataset.
candidates.time_coverage: forward-looking (event calendar) plus some historical event archive depending on plan

candidates.name: predicthq/sdk-js
candidates.what_it_holds: JavaScript/Node client (MIT, 8 stars, updated Jan 2026) for the same PredictHQ Events API described above (conferences, expos, festivals, concerts, sports, holidays, severe weather).
candidates.why_useful: Same PredictHQ event/MICE calendar access as the Python SDK, for teams preferring a JS pipeline; same paid-tier caveat.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: duplicate of predicthq/sdk-py's data source, different language binding

candidates.name: predicthq/api-specs
candidates.what_it_holds: OpenAPI specification files (MIT) enumerating the full PredictHQ API schema, including the 'conferences' and 'expos' event categories, field definitions, and rank/attendance fields.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms exactly which MICE-relevant fields (conference/expo category, predicted attendance, phq-rank) are queryable via PredictHQ before committing to build a pull -- useful as a schema reference, not itself a dataset.

candidates.name: predicthq/phq-data-science-docs
candidates.what_it_holds: PredictHQ's data-science documentation repo (MIT, 17 stars) with articles and linked downloadable Jupyter notebooks demonstrating how to build demand-forecasting features from event data (attendance impact, event density nowcasting). No committed CSV/parquet in the repo itself -- notebooks are linked externally.
candidates.why_useful: Worked methodology for turning an event calendar (including MICE/conference events) into a demand-nowcasting feature -- relevant to gap #17 (nowcasting methods) if the team ever builds an event-density regressor for business-travel markets.

candidates.name: aws-samples/demand-forecasting-on-amazon-sagemaker-with-predicthq-event-data
candidates.what_it_holds: AWS sample (MIT-0) walking through pulling PredictHQ event-impact features (including conferences/expos) and feeding them into a SageMaker demand-forecasting pipeline; includes notebook code showing the API-to-feature pipeline end to end.
candidates.why_useful: A concrete, runnable replication of turning event/conference data into a demand forecast feature -- directly usable as a template for a MICE-driven regional demand adjustment.

candidates.name: carlclabot96-ux/skywatch
candidates.what_it_holds: Small personal repo describing a 'real-time private jet tracker using ADS-B data'. No stars, unclear if data is committed vs. just a live tracker script; likely thin/individual project.
candidates.why_useful: Private/business-jet ADS-B tracking is a plausible high-end corporate-travel volume proxy (business jet movements as a leading indicator of executive/corporate travel intensity), a category with essentially no other GitHub presence found in this sweep. Flagged for the idea, not for this specific repo's maturity.
candidates.time_coverage: real-time only, no evident historical archive

notes: This theme is thin on GitHub: GBTA, Navan, TripActions, SAP Concur, MICE, 'conference calendar dataset', 'trade show calendar', 'expense report dataset', and 'corporate travel spend'/'dataset' searches all returned either zero results or pure keyword-collision noise (e.g. usernames/repos containing the literal substring 'gbta' with no relation to business-travel data). No GBTA-published index, no Concur/SAP open dataset, and no MICE-specific committed dataset exists on GitHub as far as this sweep could find -- corporate travel spend and conference attendance data appear to live entirely behind paid vendor walls (GBTA BTI, Deloitte/Certify/SAP Concur benchmark reports as PDFs, not open data). The one substantive, repeatedly-surfacing family is PredictHQ's event-intelligence API (conferences/expos/festivals/concerts by city and date, with an attendance-impact score) -- it is the closest thing to a queryable MICE/conference-calendar feed, but it is a client library over a freemium/paid API, not a free static dataset, so treat as a 'method to evaluate', not a ready-made corpus. Two GitHub API rate-limit hits (403) occurred mid-sweep on 'expense report dataset', 'trade show calendar', and 'corporate travel spend'; a 40s wait then a related-but-different query (PredictHQ) succeeded, so those three specific phrasings were never actually retried post-cooldown -- a future scout could re-run those three exact `gh search repos` queries for cheap incremental coverage. WebSearch and the github.com/search web UI (via WebFetch) were both unavailable for the entire back half of this sweep (session web-search budget exhausted; github.com/search returned 429 Retry-After 3600), so this catalogue relies on `gh search repos` coverage only -- worth a repeat pass once those channels reset. Suggest a future scout also try: 'Concur expense api', 'SAP travel expense open data', 'digital nomad visa dataset' (adjacent to gap 16), and searching by topic (`--topic=business-travel`, `--topic=mice`) once quota resets, plus checking Kaggle/Zenodo directly (out of this scout's gh-only modality) for GBTA/Deloitte business-travel-index PDF-derived datasets that a hobbyist may have transcribed.
